name: manual_ce229c
claim: When extracting a shared error-translation contextmanager for a class's transaction boundary, audit EVERY public method that opens a transaction, not just the ones already known to hit the failure mode -- lock/busy contention can surface on any write path, not only the ones that historically triggered a bug report

decisions.notes: CodeRabbit review #4989313231 on PT PR #359: only reserve() and mark_dispatch() translated a busy/locked sqlite3.OperationalError to BudgetUnavailableError; settle(), release_pre_dispatch(), and recover_expired() did not, even though _transaction()'s BEGIN IMMEDIATE means any of the five public methods can hit the same busy_timeout_ms expiry. settle() was the most exposed -- it runs after the provider spend already happened, so its caller seeing a raw sqlite3.OperationalError instead of a ledger error is a real availability/correctness gap, not cosmetic. Fixed by extracting _guarded_transaction() (wraps _transaction(), translates OperationalError, re-raises BudgetError unchanged) and switching every public method to it, not just the two that already had inline try/except. Caught by TDD retroactive-RED via monkeypatching _transaction to always raise, parametrized across the three previously-unguarded methods.
